messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed direct C-H arylation of an imidazole to form 5-(2-fluorophenyl)-1-methyl-1H-imidazole-4-carbonitrile (Shields et al., Nature 2021, reaction 3); choose the base, ligand, solvent, concentration and temperature.

Variables and options:
base:
B1: cesium pivalate [SMILES O=C([O-])C(C)(C)C.[Cs+]]
B2: potassium pivalate [SMILES O=C([O-])C(C)(C)C.[K+]]
B3: cesium acetate [SMILES O=C([O-])C.[Cs+]]
B4: potassium acetate [SMILES O=C([O-])C.[K+]]

ligand:
L1: PPhtBu2 [SMILES CC(C)(C)P(C1=CC=CC=C1)C(C)(C)C]
L2: BrettPhos [SMILES CC(C)C1=CC(C(C)C)=C(C(C(C)C)=C1)C2=C(P(C3CCCCC3)C4CCCCC4)C(OC)=CC=C2OC]
L3: X-Phos [SMILES CC(C1=C(C2=CC=CC=C2P(C3CCCCC3)C4CCCCC4)C(C(C)C)=CC(C(C)C)=C1)C]
L4: GorlosPhos HBF4 [SMILES CC(OC1=C(P(C2CCCCC2)C3CCCCC3)C(OC(C)C)=CC=C1)C]
L5: tBPh-CPhos [SMILES CN(C)C1=CC=CC(N(C)C)=C1C2=CC=CC=C2P(C(C)(C)C)C3=CC=CC=C3]
L6: PPhMe2 [SMILES CP(C)C1=CC=CC=C1]
L7: PPh2Me [SMILES CP(C1=CC=CC=C1)C2=CC=CC=C2]
L8: CgMe-PPh [SMILES C[C@]1(O2)O[C@](C[C@]2(C)P3C4=CC=CC=C4)(C)O[C@]3(C)C1]
L9: JackiePhos [SMILES FC(F)(F)C1=CC(P(C2=C(C3=C(C(C)C)C=C(C(C)C)C=C3C(C)C)C(OC)=CC=C2OC)C4=CC(C(F)(F)F)=CC(C(F)(F)F)=C4)=CC(C(F)(F)F)=C1]
L10: PPh3 [SMILES P(C1=CC=CC=C1)(C2=CC=CC=C2)C3=CC=CC=C3]
L11: P(fur)3 [SMILES P(C1=CC=CO1)(C2=CC=CO2)C3=CC=CO3]
L12: PCy3 HBF4 [SMILES P(C1CCCCC1)(C2CCCCC2)C3CCCCC3]

solvent:
S1: N,N-dimethylacetamide [SMILES CC(N(C)C)=O]
S2: p-xylene [SMILES CC1=CC=C(C)C=C1]
S3: butyronitrile [SMILES CCCC#N]
S4: n-butyl acetate [SMILES CCCCOC(C)=O]

concentration:
C1: 0.057 M
C2: 0.1 M
C3: 0.153 M

temperature:
T1: 90 °C
T2: 105 °C
T3: 120 °C

Experiments so far (best first):
B3 | L8 | S3 | C3 | T2 -> 96.4%
B3 | L8 | S3 | C2 | T3 -> 88.8%

B2 | L7 | S2 | C3 | T2 -> 0.2%

Propose exactly 20 NEW experiments not listed above. Return JSON:
{"picks": [{"base": "<label>", "ligand": "<label>", "solvent": "<label>", "concentration": "<label>", "temperature": "<label>", "reason": "<one sentence>"}]}

picks.reason: Tests whether the high-yield concentrated cesium acetate/CgMe-PPh condition benefits from a lower temperature.
Checks whether the yield continues to improve at higher temperature at the best observed concentration.
Completes a concentration-temperature comparison at low concentration to clarify their interaction.
Tests whether high temperature can compensate for the lower yield previously seen at low concentration.
Compares cesium pivalate with the best-performing cesium acetate condition at matched settings.
Tests whether potassium pivalate can retain activity with the best ligand and solvent.
Isolates the cation effect by testing potassium acetate against cesium acetate in the lead condition.
Checks whether higher temperature improves the pivalate variant while holding the other lead settings fixed.
Evaluates a higher-temperature potassium pivalate condition against the cesium acetate benchmark.
Tests whether polar aprotic DMAc supports the lead catalytic system better than butyronitrile.
Reassesses p-xylene using the successful base, ligand, and concentration combination.
Tests an ester solvent under the lead conditions to assess solvent coordination and polarity effects.
Screens bulky BrettPhos under the best base, solvent, concentration, and temperature settings.
Tests X-Phos under matched lead conditions to compare its steric and electronic profile with CgMe-PPh.
Evaluates GorlosPhos under the lead reaction conditions despite its distinct phosphonium salt form.
Screens the bulky electron-rich tBPh-CPhos ligand under the optimized reaction environment.
Tests JackiePhos in the lead condition to determine whether its highly substituted biaryl framework is beneficial.
Re-tests PPhtBu2 with the successful base and solvent to separate ligand effects from the earlier conditions.
Uses triphenylphosphine as a matched-condition reference against the strong CgMe-PPh result.
Screens the electron-rich furyl phosphine under the lead conditions to check whether it can promote this C-H arylation.
